recognize_zh: 一顆分葉核嗜中性球位於中央，周圍被約九顆紅血球緊密環繞，排列成花瓣狀的玫瑰花環（rosette）；紅血球是貼附在嗜中性球表面，而不是被吞進胞質內。
features: Central mature neutrophil with 4-5 nuclear lobes, clumped chromatin and finely granular cytoplasm
About nine red cells tightly apposed in a single circumferential ring around the neutrophil, forming a petal-like rosette
Red cells adhere to the neutrophil surface and are not engulfed (no intracytoplasmic red cells)
No platelet satellitism; single high-power field with minimal background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, high-power view, shows a mature segmented neutrophil encircled by a single ring of approximately nine red cells tightly adherent to its surface, producing a flower-like rosette. The red cells lie outside the neutrophil cytoplasm with no evidence of erythrophagocytosis, and platelet satellitism is not present. Neutrophil-erythrocyte rosettes are an in vitro phenomenon that has been linked to red cell-bound immunoglobulin or complement and to hypergammaglobulinemia; on their own they are of limited diagnostic significance but may prompt a direct antiglobulin test and review of serum proteins. Findings are consistent with erythrocyte rosette formation around a neutrophil.

ddx.vs: Platelets, not red cells, ring the neutrophils, an EDTA-dependent artifact that causes pseudothrombocytopenia.
Red cells lie inside the neutrophil or monocyte cytoplasm, often within vacuoles, rather than adherent around its perimeter.
Several neutrophils cluster around a free homogeneous LE body, the reverse arrangement of this image.
Red cells stack in linear coin-like chains unrelated to leukocytes.
